cat > c.py <<'EOF'
import bt, numpy as np
S=bt.signals(); R=bt.train_returns().astype(float); T=len(R)
sh=lambda x: x.mean()/x.std()*np.sqrt(252)
fam=np.array([s.split('_')[0] for s in S])
def consist(X,n=3):
    parts=np.array_split(X,n); s=np.array([[sh(p[:,i]) for i in range(X.shape[1])] for p in parts])
    ok=(np.sign(s)==np.sign(s[0])).all(0); return np.where(ok,np.sign(s[0]),0)
def short_hold(X): return -(fam=='hold').astype(float)
def mv(X,lam=0.5):
    mu=X.mean(0); C=np.cov(X.T); C=(1-lam)*C+lam*np.diag(np.diag(C)); return np.linalg.solve(C,mu)
# walk-forward: fit on years [0,k), test on next block
blocks=np.array_split(np.arange(T),6)
for name,f in [('consist',consist),('short_hold',short_hold),('mv',mv)]:
    out=[]
    for k in range(2,6):
        tr=np.concatenate(blocks[:k]); te=blocks[k]; w=f(R[tr]); out.append(round(sh(R[te]@w),2) if np.any(w) else None)
    w=f(R); print(name, out, 'nnz',int((w!=0).sum()), 'full-train', round(sh(R@w),2))
EOF

content.text:
I submitted a portfolio that holds all 423 signals, weighted by mean-variance optimisation on 1970–1999 data with the covariance matrix shrunk 50% toward its diagonal. Its training Sharpe is 3.68, but its validation Sharpe (2000–2012) is **−0.16**, so it did not work out of sample.

I chose it before looking at validation. No signal family held up across the training period: trend signals were positive in the 1980s and negative in the 1970s and 1990s. Shrunk mean-variance was the only method that stayed positive in all four walk-forward tests inside the training data (Sharpe 0.16–0.61). I ran the validation backtest once, on this choice only. I didn't then try other weightings against validation and keep the best, because with up to 5000 tries that would mostly fit noise and the reported number would no longer be a fair out-of-sample estimate. That means −0.16 is an honest result, not the highest validation number I could have produced. The gap from 3.68 in training shows the optimiser mostly fitted noise.
